rv.q: Too often, though, that fear diffuses into a gestural fog — a fluttering curtain, a secret door in the wall, the sound of a falling tree.
"Daphne" is so good at creating a sense of its main characters’ insularity that the production also feels confining, stuck within a set of indecipherable metaphors.
That tale of thwarted love serves as a loose inspiration for Renae Simone Jarrett's ambitious but bewildering Daphne , now receiving its world premiere at Lincoln Center.
Though appropriate to how memories and reality warp and fade in an abusive situation, these gaps make Daphne fairly thin.
In its present state, however, Daphne comes off as a wooden affair.
I regret to say that nowhere in the play are those stories and moments manifest.
There is, however, a difference between no easy answers and no answers at all, and Daphne ultimately succumbs to its pervasive mysteriousness.
The level of ambiguity in this play had the audience puzzling over plot points, trying to figure out what really happened on a very tangible level.

cn.t: Jarrett's surreal play about transformation proves more bewildering than illuminating, leaving critics confused by its dreamlike logic and unanswered questions, though some appreciate its ambitious exploration of mythology and language.
